plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. The heads track the sun when young, and the plant is widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and North America
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west each day, a movement called heliotropism, but mature flower heads stay facing east.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in southern France, England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of North America
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that produces long spires of bright magenta-pink flowers that bloom from the bottom up. It is among the first plants to colonize burned or disturbed land.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn (July to September)
plants.location: Northern temperate and subarctic regions, including Alaska, Canada, northern Europe, and Siberia
plants.funFact: Fireweed flowers open progressively up the stalk, and locals traditionally say that when the top blooms open, summer is nearly over.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree covered in fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow pom-pom flower clusters. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere's late winter, brightening the Australian bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1st.
